title: Gusto Business Compliance vs. Warp: Key Differences
summary: Gusto launched Business Compliance on Oct 1, 2026. See what it costs, what its terms say, and how Warp's AI agents handle state filings differently.
body_markdown:
Gusto Business Compliance, launched October 1, 2026, is a per-state service that handles state registrations, annual reports, and government mail for multi-state businesses. Warp takes a different approach: AI agents handle filings and resolve notices, Warp Tax Specialists take anything that needs a human, and compliance is part of the platform instead of a line item you add state by state.


The short version:


- **What Gusto sells:** a compliance service at $85 per state per month on its Simple and Plus plans. Under Gusto's Business Compliance terms, you review every filing and all government correspondence, and you remain responsible for the accuracy of everything filed.
- **What Warp does:** AI agents open the state tax accounts, file the forms, and resolve the notices. Anything that needs a human goes to Warp Tax Specialists, so it doesn't land on your team. Warp takes liability for compliance errors it’s responsible for.


## What Gusto's Business Compliance includes


This launch follows[Gusto's April 2026 acquisition of Mosey](https://www.warp.co/blog/mosey-got-acquired-by-gusto-now-what) . Gusto Business Compliance covers the paperwork around payroll in each state and is priced per state. According to Gusto's announcement and product page, it includes:


- State tax registration when you hire in a new state
- Foreign qualification for operating across state lines
- Registered agent service in each state
- Initial and annual report filing to keep you in good standing
- Government mail monitoring, with a compliance concierge team that Gusto says will read, explain, and handle agency mail
- Proactive deadline alerts


## What Gusto's terms say about responsibility


The terms are worth reading before you buy, because they define who carries the risk:


- Gusto acts as your filing agent "in an administrative capacity only," and under Gusto's Business Compliance terms, the customer is "solely responsible for ensuring that all filings are accurate, complete, and legally sufficient."
- You must review all filings submitted on your behalf and all government correspondence, and Gusto takes action on mail only where it has specifically agreed to.
- Registered agent service is provided through a third-party commercial vendor, and Gusto does not claim liability for that vendor's acts or omissions outside its reasonable control.
- Gusto's liability is capped at the amount you paid for the service in the six months before a claim.


Gusto's product page frames the service the same way: it is "operational help, not legal, tax, or regulatory advice," and "works alongside your accountant or lawyer, not in place of them."


## Where Warp is different


The difference is who finishes the job. Gusto's service files and alerts, then leaves review and required follow-up with you. Warp handles it end to end:[AI agents](https://www.warp.co/blog/ai-agents-for-hr) do the work, and anything that needs a human goes to Warp Tax Specialists, not to you.


Here is how that plays out against Gusto's new offer:


1. **Who does the work.** Gusto's terms describe it as a filing agent and put review of every filing on you. Warp's agents open the state accounts, file the forms, and resolve notices; anything that needs a human goes to Warp Tax Specialists, so the work doesn't land on your team.
2. **What expansion costs.** Gusto bills $85 per state per month on Simple or Plus. Warp pricing includes automatic state tax registration, so hiring in a new state doesn’t add a per-state line item.
3. **Who is responsible for accuracy.** Gusto's terms put accuracy on you and cap its liability at six months of fees. Warp takes liability for compliance errors it’s responsible for.
4. **What happens to agency mail.** Gusto says its concierge team will read, explain, and handle mail, but under its terms you still review all government correspondence, and Gusto acts only where it has agreed to.[Warp's agents](https://www.warp.co/agent) resolve the notice itself, and Warp Tax Specialists step in when it needs a human.


If you are already on Gusto, switching payroll providers does not mean starting over.[Warp offers white-glove migration from Gusto.](https://www.warp.co/versus/gusto)


## Which approach fits your company


Gusto Business Compliance fits a company with a small number of states, a steady headcount, and an accountant or lawyer already in place who can review filings and mail. Gusto's own page describes it as help that works alongside your advisors.


Warp fits a company that is hiring fast across states and does not want compliance to be a project. If your next hire could be in a state you have never registered in, if a tax notice arriving by mail would stall your week, or if per-state fees would climb as you expand, the model matters more than the feature list.


Questions worth asking any provider, Gusto included:


1. Who actually files, and which human responds when an agency sends a notice?
2. What happens, and who pays, if a registration or filing is missed?
3. What does the bill look like when you go from three states to ten?


## The bottom line


Gusto Business Compliance confirms what founders already feel: multi-state compliance is where growth gets slowed down. Gusto answers with a per-state service and a concierge team alongside your advisors, leaving filing accuracy and review with you. Warp answers it by having AI agents open the accounts, file the forms, and resolve notices, with Warp Tax Specialists handling anything that needs a human, so it doesn't land on your team.


If you are scaling into new states and would rather not manage compliance at all,[book a Warp demo](http://warp.co/demo/) .
